questions.question_text:
Triangle $A$ has a base of $16\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ cm}$.
Triangle $B$ has a base of $12\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $8\text{ cm}$.
Which has the larger area?

options.why: Paired $B$’s base with $A$’s height, calculating $\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times6$.
Paired $A$’s base with $B$’s height, calculating $\tfrac{1}{2}\times16\times8$.
Forgot to halve $A$’s product, comparing $16\times6$ with $\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times8$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Area of A}=16\times6\div2$
$=48\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{Area of B}=12\times8\div2$
$=48\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger: both areas are $48\text{ cm}^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
Both smaller triangles have the same perpendicular height, $9\text{ m}$.
$\text{Left area}=14\times9\div2$
$=63\text{ m}^{2}$
$\text{Right area}=6\times9\div2$
$=27\text{ m}^{2}$
$63-27=36$
The difference is $36\text{ m}^{2}$.

questions.question_text:
The right-angled triangle has perpendicular sides of length $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$.
The area of this triangle is

options.why: Added the two lengths and halved their sum: $(8+10)\div2=9$.
Multiplied the base and height but did not halve the product: $8\times10=80$.
Added the two lengths instead of multiplying and halving: $8+10=18$.

questions.solution_text:
The given sides meet at a right angle, so they are the base and height.
$\text{Area}=8\times10\div2$
$=80\div2$
$=40\text{ cm}^{2}$
